MAINTENANCE NOTES · Separate from the original visitor pages

Editing and migration notes

This static preview preserves the original website’s page structure, layout, images and wording rather than introducing a new design. These maintenance notes and the local editor are separate tools, not part of the original visitor navigation.

Update with Pages CMS

Open the Pages CMS setup and editing guide. This prototype adds GitHub-backed homepage text, repeatable upcoming events, presentation text and image uploads without changing the original visitor layout. The repository configuration and build are ready; GitHub App authorization and a first authenticated save must still be verified. No app access has been granted by adding these files.

Local preview/export tool

Open the older local content editor to preview changes in this browser and download JSON. It cannot sign in, commit, push or publish. Drafts use session storage and are not a backup. The CMS source is now in cms/*.json; an exported content.json does not replace those files. Ask a maintainer to transfer exported edits into the appropriate CMS fields.

Commit-to-publish

The existing GitHub Actions workflow compiles CMS fields into the preserved page markup, validates the result, and publishes commits to main through GitHub Pages. GitHub supplies a short-lived deployment token; there is no secret token in the visitor website. After the owner separately authorizes Pages CMS, that service can commit content changes using its repository-scoped GitHub App access. Saving a CMS change and completing deployment are separate steps.

What this preview preserves

The local visitor pages use the original source HTML, CSS and artwork. Homepage and events text can be overridden through the content file. Source wording and date ambiguities are preserved, not silently rewritten or corrected. A listing without a year should not be assumed to be an upcoming event.

Squarespace features and remaining dependencies

  • Visual editing: this is not the Squarespace dashboard. The Pages CMS prototype edits defined content fields; the older local tool remains preview/export only. Neither rearranges the original page layout.
  • Contact form: the Squarespace form is removed and clearly labeled unsupported on the contact page. No messages are submitted or forwarded. A replacement form service and confirmed delivery destination would be needed.
  • Newsletter: the Squarespace subscription widget is removed and clearly labeled unsupported. No subscriber data is collected or forwarded. A mailing-list provider would need to be connected separately.
  • Instagram: the original image grid is a frozen snapshot, not a live feed. New posts will not appear automatically without an integration.
  • Events and calendar downloads: legacy event-detail links remain on the original site; Squarespace ICS downloads are disabled and labeled unsupported. They are not fully migrated. Preserving downloadable calendars requires a complete export or a replacement with confirmed dates, times and timezones.
  • Media embeds: original third-party provider embeds depend on those providers, their availability and visitor privacy settings. Squarespace account functionality is not reproduced by copying page HTML.
  • Shopping cart: the original Squarespace cart is disabled and labeled unsupported. No cart or checkout backend is provided.
  • Book purchases: original outbound purchase links remain external. No new checkout or payment system is provided.
  • Full archive and redirects: this is not a complete migration of every original URL. The source inventory records the original sitemap. Review missing pages and legacy links before changing the domain.
  • SEO, analytics, domain and email: this preview is excluded from indexing. A real launch needs reviewed indexing settings, redirects and analytics, plus deliberate domain/DNS changes that preserve email records.

Recommendation

A static site can suit homepage and events updates with an authenticated content editor, once its access and publishing flow are tested. Squarespace may still be worth the quoted $230/year if integrated visual editing, forms, mailing tools and vendor support are important. That renewal quote is supplied by Josh, not independently verified; domain registration and optional services are separate costs. Do not cancel the original service until all needed pages, forms, feeds and calendar links have replacements and have been tested.

Source and ownership

View the website source on GitHub. Original images, styles and fonts are included in the repository and served locally. The project started from Drew’s website repository; the fidelity revision uses Josh’s original public website as the reference. Artwork and original text remain their owners’ work. No original repository branch, domain or subscription was changed.
